# M0-a-04 — the closing check's notes (not failing lines)

These notes come from the closing check of item M0-a-04 (lane `check/M0-a-04-close-r1`, 2026-10-04). Under the
session's rulings J162 and J169, the closing check fails the item only on a blocker. Neither finding below is a
blocker: one is a hardening fixture for a path the code already gets right, and the other names the reader a fix-round
change leaves to a later item. Each row names its handling and where it belongs. The verdict and its evidence are in
`checks/M0-a-04.md` (the closing round is at the top).

The first check's notes N-1 – N-5 stay in `checks/M0-a-04.md`. N-1 (the placement's fallback moves an incoming vertex
metres, beyond *Existing geometry wins*' √2 · `attractCm` and its acute-tip bound) is now recorded by C-0170 (1) as
the design's own fallback text; it is still the session's to route to the design's reviewer and to M0-a-05, whose step 3
re-enters the fallback's new segments. The ids below continue that numbering.

**Session fix round S3 (N-55 (5) and N-53 (4)'s follow-on N-s1-4) — the closing check's notes (lane

| id | observation | suggested handling | milestone |
|---|---|---|---|
| N-11 | **Mutant MA4 survives: no pin holds "throws before it plans, reads or charges anything" (C-0294 (1)).** MA4 moves `splitThrough`'s closed check from its entry to after `planSplitThrough` (just before `applySplitPlan`). It survives `splitThrough.test.ts` (`Tests 29 passed (29)`), because every closed-overlay pin uses a lawful point, which still throws under MA4 with the arena bit-identical and the version unchanged. MA4 is not equivalent. The checker's mirror probe (overlays kept from a committed, a rejected and a threw batch on QUARTERS at L2) shows the difference. On the tree, a point outside the lattice (`{x: 1e15, y: 150}`) throws `insert: the transaction is closed (committed or rejected)` and the overlay's `work.total` stays unchanged on both calls. Under MA4, the same call returns the typed refusal `E_OUT_OF_RANGE`, and a lawful split charges 3 to the closed overlay's work before it throws. In both cases the arena is bit-identical and the version is unchanged. So the fixed code keeps C-0294 (1)'s "never a typed refusal" and "before it plans, reads or charges anything" (CONFIRMED). Under the mutant, nothing is written either way, so the untested direction stays fail-safe. | Add one pin to the N-55 (5) describe: on each closed overlay, a split at a point the plan would refuse (outside the lattice, or E_LEVEL on a finer edge) throws the closed message, and `o.work.total` is unchanged after a lawful attempt. | M4 (or M0-a-04's next round, if one opens) |
| N-12 | **`attractVertex` / `attractRun` write silently on a closed overlay.** C-0294 (1) names them as internal step helpers without a check of their own, with `insertChain` (M0-a-05 round s7) as their door. The checker's mirror probe calls `attractVertex(o, pt(505, 120))` on the same three closed overlays. That is a write outside any transaction: Q13's class, through a door the ruling did not name. Nothing in the tree calls them with a stale overlay: no caller outside the kernel, and the façade (`facade/kernel.ts`) does not expose them. Only a programming error in a future caller can reach it, so it is a contrived-writer escape (N-45), not a blocker of this round. | Either put the same one-line `check(tx.closed !== true, 'the transaction is closed (committed or rejected)')` at the entry of `attractVertex` and `attractRun`, with the same closed-overlay pins, or have the session rule that the barrel exports are internal and drop them from the barrel.
